prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a parking lot collision in Pasadena, Texas, and has neck strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1255; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This call is being recorded for claim file purposes. Can you please state your full name for the record?

A: Sure. I'd rather not give my full name on a recording, so just put down that I'm the driver of the vehicle involved.

Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where the collision happened?

A: It was in a shopping center parking lot in Pasadena, Texas. I was pulling out of a space near the main entrance.

Q: What were you doing right before the impact?

A: I had checked my mirror, saw the lane was clear, and started backing out slowly. The other car came from my right side, going pretty fast down the aisle, and hit the rear quarter panel of my car.

Q: Were you moving when the impact happened?

A: Yes, I was rolling backward at maybe three or four miles an hour.

Q: Did you notice any injuries right after the collision?

A: My neck felt stiff almost immediately. I didn't think much of it at first, but by the next morning I had a dull ache across the back of my neck and some tightness going up into my head.

Q: Have you sought any medical treatment since the collision?

A: Yes, I went to urgent care the following day. They diagnosed a neck strain and gave me a muscle relaxer and told me to rest and use ice.

Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?

A: Some days are better than others. Turning my head to the left is the hardest part, and I've had trouble sleeping a few nights.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: No, I think that covers it. I just want my car repaired and my neck to get back to normal.

Q: Thank you for your cooperation. We'll be in touch with next steps.
